title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) Principles for Microservices
description: Master Strategic and Tactical Domain-Driven Design, Bounded Contexts, Aggregates, Value Objects, Domain Events, and Clean Hexagonal Architecture in Go.
body: Structure complex enterprise microservices without cluttering business logic with SQL queries or HTTP web framework details. Learn DDD strategic context mapping, aggregate roots, value objects, and hexagonal ports & adapters.

sections.title: Section 1: DDD Strategic Patterns & Bounded Contexts

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: Bounded Contexts & Ubiquitous Language
lessons.body:
### The Scenario: Misaligned Terminology
In an e-commerce organization, the Sales team defines an 'Account' as a billing target, while the Security team defines 'Account' as an authentication login identity. When developers combine both into a single giant database table, every feature update breaks adjacent team code.

### Strategic Solution: Bounded Contexts
Structure your system into decoupled **Bounded Contexts** with explicit boundaries and domain-specific Ubiquitous Language.

sections.title: Section 2: Tactical DDD Patterns (Aggregates, Entities & Value Objects)

lessons.title: Lesson 2.1: Designing Pure Aggregate Roots & Immutable Value Objects in Go
Lesson 2.2: Emitting Domain Events for Async Decoupling
lessons.body:
### Decoupling Secondary Actions
When an `Article` state transitions to `PUBLISHED`, avoid calling email notification services or search indexers directly inside the aggregate. Emit a `DomainEvent` (`ArticlePublishedEvent`) to be processed asynchronously.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.1: Structuring Hexagonal Go Directory Layouts
lessons.body:
### Layer Isolation Rules
- **`domain/`**: Pure Go models and interfaces. ZERO third-party dependencies.
- **`usecase/`**: Business application workflow coordinators.
- **`infrastructure/`**: Database SQL queries, HTTP handlers, and external API clients.
